subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Does the runtime-aligned trusted-proxy readiness probe provide the intended security-diagnostic policy for exposed Gateway deployments, including Doctor’s explicit opt-in execution of active exec SecretRefs?
rationale: This changes when an exposed Gateway moves from an unauthenticated critical finding to a trusted-proxy warning; code review can verify contract alignment, but the accepted security posture and operator-action boundary require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the diagnostic boundary
options.body: Accept the runtime-aligned warning path after source review and completion of the required current-head checks.

options.title: Keep all trusted-proxy exposure critical
options.body: Retain the existing conservative Doctor classification until a broader trusted-proxy security policy is approved.

options.title: Narrow the acceptance criteria
options.body: Require an additional documented or tested reverse-proxy-origin contract before allowing the warning path.

recommendation.title: Approve the diagnostic boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the runtime-aligned warning path after source review and completion of the required current-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the most direct supplied history on the proposed diagnostic and can answer implementation-specific questions while a gateway-security owner makes the policy decision.
